Stage 1 component distributions. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. (A) Component 1
sample-coordinate distribution. (B) Component 2 sample-coordinate distribution. Facets show
components 1-2 in decomposition order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate
distributions; fine rugs show sample coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero. Categorical
metadata is shown by restrained density fills and solid outlines; reference rugs occupy the
upper margin and focal rugs the lower margin. The analysis unit is independent biological
observation; the design is cross-sectional; the estimand is the descriptive distribution of
sample coordinates. No component-selection threshold is applied. This descriptive gallery does
not rank or nominate a biological coordinate.
Stage 1 component distributions. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. (A) Component 1
sample-coordinate distribution. (B) Component 2 sample-coordinate distribution. Facets show
components 1-2 in decomposition order; stored densities summarize sample-coordinate
distributions; fine rugs show sample coordinates; dotted vertical lines mark zero. Continuous
metadata is shown by fine sample rugs with a perceptually ordered colour and opacity scale. The
analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive distribution of sample coordinates. No component-selection
threshold is applied. This descriptive gallery does not rank or nominate a biological
coordinate.
Stage 1 decomposition coordinates. The figure uses molecular layers layer 1, layer 2. (A) layer
1 molecular-layer coordinates. (B) layer 2 molecular-layer coordinates. Facets identify
molecular layers; points show component 1 sample coordinates rank-ordered within each layer;
the dotted horizontal line marks zero. Point colours and point shapes encode categorical
planted group. The subtitle reports the stored synthetic ground-truth angle for component 1.
The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the descriptive sample coordinate on component 1. No component-selection threshold
is applied. This display does not select a component or establish biological interpretation.

1 molecular-layer coordinates. (B) layer 2 molecular-layer coordinates. Facets identify

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses molecular layers layer 1, layer 2.
The black curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component
1. Reference rugs occupy the upper margin and focal rugs the lower margin; grey and red
redundantly identify categorical planted group. Critical-point symbols and position guides are
omitted. The analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is
cross-sectional; the estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the selected
component. No calibrated critical-point or barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an
exploratory description and does not by itself establish a biological state transition.

The black curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component
1. Fine rug colour and opacity identify continuous observed time. Critical-point symbols and

Density-derived quasi-potential landscape. The figure uses layer 1 molecular data. The black
curve shows U(x) = -log p(x), derived from the stored density estimate for component 1.
Reference rugs occupy the upper margin and focal rugs the lower margin; grey and red
redundantly identify categorical planted group. Small open circles mark stored stable wells
directly on the curve. Small red diamonds mark stored unstable barriers directly on the curve.
Fine grey dashed lines locate stored critical-point positions. The vertical display is focused
on the stored critical-point range; higher low-density tails continue beyond the panel. The
analysis unit is independent biological observation; the design is cross-sectional; the
estimand is the density-derived quasi-potential along the selected component. Critical-point
classifications are point estimates without uncertainty. No calibrated critical-point or
barrier threshold is applied. The landscape is an exploratory description and does not by
itself establish a biological state transition.
